rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2, a field experiment (2017-2018) in a 0.5 ha nectarine orchard with a capacitance-probe-triggered PDI treatment vs an ETc-scheduled control, four replications each. Q2: Section 3.1 and Figure 2B, in-line water meters recorded 420.4 mm (control) vs 251.6 mm (PDI), a mean water reduction of about 40%; Conclusions restate that SWC-based PDI used 40% less irrigation than the traditionally scheduled treatment. Q4: Section 2.2 and Figures 1, 2C, soil water content in 0-0.5 m measured continuously by the capacitance probes was used to trigger/stop irrigation at the threshold values, and REW in PDI was reduced by up to 15% (postharvest) and 4% (fruit growth) relative to control, i.e. the intermediate soil-water variable through which the sensor system reduces applied water was measured.
rows.notes: Water saving measured by one method (in-line water meters) only; single site, single orchard of one cultivar, one growing season; no dispersion reported for applied irrigation volumes (seasonal totals only). The conclusion that threshold-SWC scheduling could be promising 'in clay-loam soils in Mediterranean areas' is a scope qualifier rather than an explicitly stated requirement, so Q7 is no. No limitations stated specifically about the water-saving result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2, own field experiment comparing sensor-based PDI with ETc-scheduled control in a nectarine orchard. Q2: Section 3.3 and Table 1, no significant differences between control and PDI for yield (8.37 vs 6.24 t/ha, ns), number of fruits, fruit mass and crop load; Conclusions state 40% less irrigation with no penalty in yield. Q4: Sections 3.2 and 3.4, Figures 2C and 3, the study measured soil water content/REW and plant water status (midday stem water potential, gas exchange) showing only a moderate deficit in PDI (mean <U+03A8>stem 0.25 MPa lower than control), the intermediate variables linking the sensor-based scheduling to maintained yield. Q9: Table 1 reports yield and yield components as means <U+00B1> SE (n = 4 replicates).
rows.notes: Yield difference was not statistically significant but PDI yield was numerically ~25% lower (6.24 vs 8.37 t/ha) with n = 4 and cracking slightly higher in PDI; the 'no yield penalty' claim rests on a non-significant difference with low replication. Yield assessed by one method (harvest weighing) at one site, one cultivar, one harvest season. The authors note their yields were lower than those of de la Rosa et al. probably due to management (thinning) differences and that crop WUE was not increased because of cracking, but these are explanations/comparisons rather than explicitly stated limitations of the yield result, so Q8 is answered no with doubt. No explicit stated requirements for the effect (Q7).

notes: Full text appears complete (some figure captions duplicated by PDF extraction). The study's main focus is comparing terrestrial and remote water-status indicators; the water saving and yield results are reported as secondary own results of the same experiment.
